metadata.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine
top_takeaways: Optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women require attention to sex-specific hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health domains across the life course.

The Female Life Stage construct defines 4 distinct stages—perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)—along with pregnancy as a unique modifying life event to guide targeted screening and treatment.
Overcoming fragmented healthcare and inconsistent guideline alignment across specialties is essential to improve cardiovascular outcomes and clinical workflows for female patients.

recommendations.statement: Implement female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations across the 4 distinct Female Life Stages (perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, and postmenopause) to address interconnected hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health domains.
recommendations.target_population: Girls and women across the life course

recommendations.target_population: Females with a history of pregnancy or adverse pregnancy outcomes
